scenarios.name: Scenario 1
scenarios.title: 8 fields + 2 minis
scenarios.description: Each winter pitch split into four 6v6 fields (Fields 1–8), plus Minis 1–2.
pros: Each comp plays at the same time each week
Field rotation allows the pitch to recover after getting a lot of action
Don't have to communicate changes to people who have already been told about field sizes
cons: Smaller than recommended field sizes (according to Northern NSW recommendations)
Less room for players means less ball time and faster-paced games — more tackles as players have less room to find space
More refs required for a single game — Monday needs 7 refs and 5 of them get a single game (Tuesday: 5 refs, 1 gets a single game)

scenarios.name: Scenario 2
scenarios.title: 6 fields + 2 minis
scenarios.description: Each winter pitch split into three even fields running across it (Fields 1–6), plus Minis 1–2.
pros: Most refs get two games — Monday needs 5 refs instead of 7, and 4 of them get two games (Tuesday: 5 refs, 4 get two games)
Fields meet Northern NSW recommended sizes
More space = a slower-paced game with fewer tackles, more time for players to think on the ball and fewer close-range shots on goal
The fields feel more full, good for the atmosphere of feeling like a “complete” comp (e.g. compared to mixed teams coming down to an empty rec oval and playing in a small corner)
cons: Senior teams might alternate between waves (wave 1 this week, wave 2 next)
Different field size to what was communicated to some players
Fields don't get as much of a break (though there are fewer people per m²)
